tickerText: [TENNIS] Challenger Sunday brought five new crowns: Dylan Dietrich won his third title in four events with a 6-1, 6-2 final over Liam Draxl in Drummondville, while Passaro, Samuel, Seyboth Wild and Watanuki also finished on top • [SQUASH] Joel Makin defended the Pittsburgh Open by rallying from two games down to beat Marwan ElShorbagy 8-11, 9-11, 12-10, 11-5, 11-7, and the 2026–27 PSA World Championships head to London's British Airways ARC from March 27 with a record $1.5 million purse • [BADMINTON] Syed Modi India International Super 300 began in Lucknow with rising Indian stars Tanvi Sharma and Unnati Hooda in action as Indonesia locked three Hangzhou Finals spots for Alwi Farhan, Fajar/Fikri and Tiwi/Fadia • [PICKLEBALL] Championship Sunday at Proton Daytona Beach saw Hunter Johnson beat Federico Staksrud for men's singles, Judit Castillo take women's singles, Johns/Waters win mixed, Bright/Waters stretch their streak to 19 straight titles, and Ge/JW Johnson defend men's doubles • [TABLE TENNIS] Muscat closed the WTT Finals race as Togami won Star Contender singles and Hong Kong's full fields were set with Matsushima topping the men's standings, Wang Manyu and Honoka Hashimoto among the women, and Wang Chuqin/Sun Yingsha taking mixed wild card at Kai Tak Dec. 9–13

newsItems.title: Dietrich's Third In Four
newsItems.excerpt: Virginia alum Dylan Dietrich captured his third ATP Challenger title in four appearances Sunday in Drummondville, rolling past Canada's Liam Draxl 6-1, 6-2 to climb to a career-high No. 155.

newsItems.title: Lucknow Draws Open
newsItems.excerpt: The Syed Modi India International Super 300 kicked off Tuesday in Lucknow with Tanvi Sharma, Unnati Hooda, Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand leading a deep Indian contingent at the BWF World Tour stop.

newsItems.title: Hong Kong Fields Set
newsItems.excerpt: WTT confirmed all 32 singles players for Finals Hong Kong after Star Contender Muscat, with Sora Matsushima leading the men's race, seven Chinese women qualified, and Sabine Winter and Joo Cheonhui sealing the last women's berths.

newsItems.title: Daytona Streak Hits 19
newsItems.excerpt: Anna Bright and Anna Leigh Waters won their 19th consecutive women's doubles title at the Proton Daytona Beach Open, while Hunter Johnson, Judit Castillo and defending pair Augie Ge and JW Johnson swept the other finals.
